why: The statement asks only whether cluster primes are infinite. The 1999 and 2003 papers bound the count from above (and show the reciprocal sum converges), which constrains the set's size without settling infinitude; both are pre-snapshot journal papers, so bound/digested. Close call: an upper bound on the count does not push toward either answer on infinitude, so 'none' was also defensible; 'bound' was chosen as it moves a quantity on the problem, and both are pre-snapshot so the choice does not affect the outcome. Shehu–Uka claims an unbounded difference-of-primes statement, a different question (variant), with an undatable claim. Gafni–Tao concerns rough numbers in prime gaps, a neighbouring problem (variant). The Lean file is a formal statement only (none). AlphaProof Nexus attempted #17 and produced nothing; an unsuccessful attempt carries no mathematics, so scope none and AI role none.
doubts: The Althöfer PDF 'erdos cluster findings' was never read and could hold an in-window, possibly AI-assisted, result; the record cannot rule this out. Elsholtz's constant (1/8 vs 1/60) is unresolved but irrelevant to the outcome.
